summary: Former lookout site on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation, Apache County, AZ; FFLA lists it gone and Forest Lookouts removed. No build, staffing or fire sources found.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks it removed, FFLA lists it gone, and the Peakbagging table labels the site as one where the building has been removed

evidence.supports: names the Fort Apache Indian Reservation as the land the site sits on
Apache County; listed as Ground and Gone; coordinates
table spells the name Bonito Rock, labelled LO site
latitude token matches the association's coordinates
longitude token matches the association's coordinates
BM means elevation read from a nearby benchmark survey disk, the contrast with the interpreted-from-contours method
LO site means building removed and maybe no evidence remaining
evidence.quote: has been removed and there may be no evidence remaining

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Peakbagging table spells the name Bonito Rock; its coordinates match the association's 33.78047, -109.61664, so the two entries are treated as one lookout

notes_for_editor: Three sources agree the lookout is gone or removed, and the Peakbagging coordinates match the record. Not found in any source read: build date, staffing, fires, or whether the public may visit. The record's access level permission and its note 'On tribal land. Ask the tribe before visiting.' are not backed by any source read; verify or drop. Peakbagging gives 8780 ft, interpolated from contours, which could be considered for elevation_m. Two web searches returned only unrelated entries. None of the three is on the FFLOS Arizona register, which lists only Barfoot and Mormon Lake. Fact-check 2026-10-10: no page read mentions visiting, access or permission; the story gives only general advice to ask permission, on reservation land.
